brief: AI investment and record US corporate profits, the highest GDP share since WWII, have let equities absorb an energy shock, higher yields and renewed Fed hikes, but TSL expects 2027 profit growth to slow as AI capex growth peaks just as employment recovers, lifting unit labor costs and squeezing margins. October payrolls rose 165k, reinforcing TSL's base case of quarterly Fed hikes beyond Q1 2027, with the terminal rate higher than markets expect if AI momentum holds. Over 80% of estimated AI ecosystem revenue still comes from recycled capex rather than outside customers, and Chinese open-weight-model competition is pressuring token prices. An AI investment reversal would hit markets, but TSL's central forecast is not an abrupt collapse: fallout would stay contained, up to 800,000 jobs lost and unemployment up about 0.5 points, given the buildout's import intensity, though equity losses and credit stress would still trigger a recession. Democrats' midterm sweep of Congress raises fiscal-brinkmanship risk and resistance to AI infrastructure. Lula's re-election selloff in Brazil is framed as an entry point. BoJ and Fed hiking cycles have further to run. ECB and BoE face tighter constraints. Oil's central case is retreat toward $80/bbl as Hormuz escalation stays contained.
